walkthrough:
Set up simultaneous equations using $f\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 5$ and $f(\pi) = 11$:
$$a + b\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 5 \implies a + \frac{1}{2}b = 5$$
$$a + b\cos(\pi) = 11 \implies a - b = 11$$

Subtract the second equation from the first to solve for $b$:
$$\left(a + \frac{1}{2}b\right) - (a - b) = 5 - 11 \implies \frac{3}{2}b = -6 \implies b = -4$$

Substitute $b = -4$ into $a - b = 11$ to find $a$:
$$a - (-4) = 11 \implies a + 4 = 11 \implies a = 7$$
$$a = 7, \quad b = -4$$

hints: Find range of $f(x) = 7 - 4\cos x$ using $-1 \le \cos x \le 1$.
walkthrough:
Determine the minimum and maximum values of $f(x) = 7 - 4\cos x$ on $[0, 2\pi]$:
$$\text{Minimum} = 7 - 4(1) = 3$$
$$\text{Maximum} = 7 - 4(-1) = 11$$
$$\text{Range of } f: \quad 3 \le f(x) \le 11$$

State the set of values of $k$ lying outside the range where $f(x) = k$ has no solution:
$$k < 3 \quad \text{or} \quad k > 11$$
